text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging | cont-batch: p99 latency spike detected on streaming path. SLO breach threshold breached for US-WEST. Auto-alert to oncall.

maria (oncall): I’m on it. Any idea customer impact yet? Which models?

aj: quick numbers — p95 ~ 420ms -> 560ms, p99 jumped from ~1.2s to 4.6s over last 10m. Streaming stall rate +320%. Errors ~0.4% (transient stream disconnects). Affected tag: rwd-7b-v2-family and a couple of quantized variants.

sahil: seeing KV cache evictions spike at the same time on the cont-batch nodes: eviction rate from 3/s -> 48/s. Likely repeated cold starts for long sessions.

jen: sampled a few requests on the hot queue — lots of mixed seqlen payloads. Batches are getting padded to long lengths and then streaming stalls when a huge example is stitched in the batch. Paste logs:```
# tail -n 60 /var/log/contbatch/serve.log
[12:04:01] req=42abc seq_len=64
[12:04:01] req=42abd seq_len=4096 <-- big outlier
[12:04:02] batch=8 tokens=32768 exec_ms=4580
[12:04:02] stall_detected stream_id=xyz
```

kevin: padding amplification. We’ve seen this amplify tail latency before when mixed short+very-long examples hit the same scheduler window. Scheduler fairness currently uses oldest-first but not strict per-seqlen isolation.

maria (oncall): OK we need a fast mitigation path. Options?

aj: immediate options (fastest -> slower):
- throttle max_batch_tokens to 8k on US-WEST cont-batch pool (config change, immediate).
- enable preemptive streaming path for queued streaming requests (bypass heavy batching when seq_len variance > threshold).
- enable per-customer concurrent-stream limit for large customers (soft limit) to avoid noisy neighbors.
- fallback routing for rwd-7b-v2 -> rwd-7b-v2-streaming-optimized (smaller KV footprint).

jen: configs I can flip quickly: `max_batch_tokens: 8192`, `batch_window_ms: 8` for streaming queues. Also `seqlen_outlier_threshold: 2048` to route outliers to a separate fastpath.

kevin: downside: reducing max_batch_tokens will increase cost and maybe reduce throughput, but will shave p99 significantly.

ops-bot: runbook step triggered: `opsctl set-config --cluster contbatch-usw2 --key max_batch_tokens --value 8192 --override`

aj: I’m going to apply `max_batch_tokens=8192` on the two most-impacted shards now. Will monitor p99.

(1 minute later)
aj: Applied config on shard-07 and shard-09. Rolling apply so not to crush capacity.

(2 minutes later)
aj: p99 dropped from 4.6s -> 1.4s on shards updated. Global p99 now ~1.8s, still slightly above SLO but much better. Streaming stalls down ~65%.

maria (oncall): Good. Sahil, can you dig into why the KV evictions spiked at scale? Could be memory pressure or a bug in cache sizing.

sahil: preliminary — memory pressure correlates with a new model variant that has a larger KV per-layer footprint; combined with giant batches we hit the eviction threshold faster. I’ll open an infra issue.

customer-success: Heads-up — we have two customers who saw degraded streams: AcmePay and Veridian. AcmePay has a live payments demo and is sensitive. We should send an incident update if we expect longer mitigation.

maria (oncall): Agreed. I’ll draft a quick customer note after we stabilize. For now prioritize containment + fallback routing.

jen: Next mitigation I’ll stage: enable `seqlen_outlier_fastpath=true` which routes any request with initial token count > 2048 to a preemptive streaming lane that uses smaller batching and avoids KV eviction pressure. I’ll canary that on shard-09.

aj: Canaries look clean on shard-09 after fastpath enabled. p99 on canary shard is 370ms.

kevin: Follow-ups we need to track:
- short-term: keep `max_batch_tokens=8192` until end of day, schedule rolling restart only if nodes show memory leaks (sahil).
- medium: add seqlen-based scheduling fairness (prefer small seqlen when mixed batches detected) — research task.
- long-term: adapt scheduler to dynamic batch shaping and KV-aware placement, and add per-model KV footprint metadata to admission control.

maria (oncall): Customer note drafted: "We detected elevated streaming latency in US-WEST impacting a subset of customers. Mitigations applied (batch cap + fastpath). Most customers restored; AcmePay/Veridian experienced brief degraded sessions. Root cause: mixed sequence-length batches causing padding amplification + KV eviction. We'll follow up with RCA." Will send to CS once oncall green.

customer-success: Please cc our AE for AcmePay (sylvia) and mark priority-high.

maria (oncall): handing to aj for overnight monitoring. I’ll be offline in 30m — leaving these action items:
- aj: watch p99 and streaming stall rate, rollback cap if it causes unacceptable throughput drop.
- sahil: open infra ticket for KV eviction spike + memory footprint analysis.
- jen: run medium-term canary of `seqlen_outlier_fastpath` across 10% of shards tomorrow.
- kevin: prioritize scheduler fairness spike mitigation on the backlog.

aj: ACK. I’ll post status updates in this thread every 30m and escalate if p99 > 2s for >10m.

maria (oncall): Thanks team. Incident classified as P2 for now. Will convert to P1 if repeated regressions or customer impact extends. :white_check_mark:

(End of thread)"
